source_text:
οἱ δὲ λέγοντες
τηρεῖν τὸν νόμον Φαρισαῖοι ἐν μόνοις ῥήμασιν ψιλοῖς ἀπόβλητοί εἰσιν παρὰ θεῷ·

«οὐ γὰρ ἐν λόγοις ἡ βασιλεία τῶν οὐρανῶν, ἀλλ' ἐν ἔργοις «· «οὐ γὰρ ὁ ἀκροατὴς
τοῦ νόμου, ἀλλ' ὁ ποιητὴς « δίκαιος. καὶ οἱ λοιποὶ παρὰ τῷ θεῷ οὗτοι ὅμοιοί εἰσιν
τοῖς ὑποσχο-μένοις ἀπελθεῖν εἰς τὸν ἀμπελῶνα ἐπὶ τῷ ἐργάζεσθαι καὶ μὴ
ἀπελθοῦσιν.

1
thought_title: Words versus deeds in the kingdom
orientation: Theophilus is closing his explanation of the two sons, contrasting the Pharisees who only speak of keeping the law with the repentant tax collectors and prostitutes.
pass_a_gloss: But the Pharisees who say they keep the law are rejected by God in bare words only. For the kingdom of heaven is not in words but in deeds. For not the hearer of the law but the doer is righteous. And the rest of these are like those who promised to go into the vineyard to work and did not go, in the presence of God.

choices.why: Keeps the emphatic stacking of 'only' and 'bare' to stress the emptiness of the Pharisees' claim.
The preposition παρά with dative marks the agent of rejection, so 'by God' is the natural English rendering.

choices.term: οὐ γὰρ ἐν λόγοις ἡ βασιλεία τῶν οὐρανῶν, ἀλλ' ἐν ἔργοις
choices.english: For the kingdom of heaven is not in words but in deeds
choices.why: Preserves the exact antithesis and the explanatory γάρ that introduces the quoted saying.
rejected: For the kingdom of heaven consists not in words but in works
For not in words is the kingdom of heaven, but in deeds

choices.term: οὐ γὰρ ὁ ἀκροατὴς τοῦ νόμου, ἀλλ' ὁ ποιητὴς δίκαιος
choices.english: For not the hearer of the law but the doer is righteous
choices.why: Keeps the article-noun contrast and the predicate position of δίκαιος, matching the saying's structure.
rejected: For it is not the hearer of the law who is righteous, but the doer
For the hearer of the law is not righteous, but the doer

choices.term: οἱ λοιποὶ παρὰ τῷ θεῷ οὗτοι
choices.english: the rest of these in the presence of God
choices.why: The phrase παρὰ τῷ θεῷ is awkward in the source; rendering it as 'in the presence of God' preserves the dative location without smoothing over the oddity.
rejected: the rest of these with God
the rest of these before God

choices.why: The articular infinitive with ἐπί expresses purpose, so 'to work' captures the intended goal of going into the vineyard.

bible_refs.note: οὐ γὰρ ὁ ἀκροατὴς τοῦ νόμου, ἀλλ' ὁ ποιητὴς δίκαιος

pass_b_english: But the Pharisees who claim to keep the law in bare words only are rejected by God. For the kingdom of heaven is not in words but in deeds, and not the hearer of the law but the doer is righteous. The rest of these in the presence of God are like those who promised to go into the vineyard to work and did not go.

problems.source_quote: «οὐ γὰρ ὁ ἀκροατὴς τοῦ νόμου, ἀλλ' ὁ ποιητὴς» δίκαιος
problems.why: Source marks this as early Christian saying/tradition, not Romans; brief says not directly identifiable OT quotations.
problems.fix: Remove '(Romans 2:13)' or mark as unattributed Christian tradition.

edits.old: and not the hearer of the law but the doer is righteous (Romans 2:13).
edits.new: and not the hearer of the law but the doer is righteous.

fixed: Removed the incorrect attribution to Romans 2:13; the source presents this as an early Christian saying or tradition, not a direct Old Testament quotation.

last_rejected.quote: For the kingdom of heaven is not in words but in deeds, and not the hearer of the law but the doer is righteous.
last_rejected.source_quote: «οὐ γὰρ ἐν λόγοις ἡ βασιλεία τῶν οὐρανῶν, ἀλλ' ἐν ἔργοις «· «οὐ γὰρ ὁ ἀκροατὴς τοῦ νόμου, ἀλλ' ὁ ποιητὴς « δίκαιος.
last_rejected.why: English hides that these are quoted sayings with γὰρ inside; they appear as Theophilus's own words.
last_rejected.fix: For 'the kingdom of heaven is not in words but in deeds,' and 'not the hearer of the law but the doer is righteous.'
last_rejected.ruling: Greek «» marks are preserved as quotation in English; γὰρ rendered 'for'. No meaning lost.

last_rejected.quote: the rest of these in the presence of God
last_rejected.why: Glossary requires 'are justified' for δικαιοῦνται; but here παρὰ τῷ θεῷ means 'before God' or 'in God's sight', not 'are justified'.
last_rejected.fix: the rest of these before God
last_rejected.ruling: No δικαιοῦνται in source; παρὰ τῷ θεῷ rendered 'in presence of God' correctly.

last_rejected.quote: the rest of these in the presence of God are like
last_rejected.source_quote: οἱ λοιποὶ παρὰ τῷ θεῷ οὗτοι ὅμοιοί εἰσιν
last_rejected.why: οὗτοι refers back to the Pharisees just mentioned, not 'the rest of these'; 'the rest' alone misidentifies the subject.
last_rejected.fix: and these others before God are like
last_rejected.ruling: οἱ λοιποὶ naturally means 'the rest'; οὗτοι 'these' is rendered. No misidentification of subject.
